newsitem.title: UK: Building societies welcome draft UK law.
newsitem.headline: Building societies welcome draft UK law.

text.p: Britain's Building Societies Association on Wednesday welcomed the government's revised draft Building Societies Bill and encouraged its early introduction to Parliament.
"Building societies will warmly welcome today's proposals which, if enacted, will remove the restrictions on their activities embodied in the 1986 Act," said BSA chairman Brian Davis in a statement.

Davis, who is also chief executive of the Nationwide Building Society, said the BSA fully supports what he called the Treasury's "thoughtful compromise" on the question of protection from takeover for those societies that convert to bank status and float on the stock exchange.
"They will lose this protection only if they acquire another financial institution, or if the overwhelming majority of their shareholders vote to remove the protection," Davis said.
It is doubtful that the proposed legislation will be passed in the life of this parliament.
A general election is due by May of next year and the proposal was not included in the Queen's Speech, which sets out the government's legislative programme for the session.
The Treasury has said that it still hopes to find a slot for the bill in the parliamentary agenda especially as it expects the legislation to be non-controversial.
